sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Interactive Lab 1: The Zero Trust Blast Radius and Incident Response Studio. Switch between Flat, DMZ, and Zero Trust micro-segmented topologies, choose a compromised ingress node, and execute emergency containment protocols to verify graph blast radius limits and projected equity depreciation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Let's test the Zero Trust Studio! Switch between Preset 1 for flat perimeter collapse and Preset 3 for strict micro-segmentation—watch how Blast Radius drops below 15 percent and protects both databases!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Formative Checkpoint 1: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies and Blast Radius Minimization. Which Kubernetes configuration prevents a compromised analytics pod from scanning database subnets inside a cluster?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1 time, Kaito! A compromised Python microservice is running inside Kubernetes. What YAML policy shuts down east-west database probing?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Enforcing a Default-Deny NetworkPolicy with an empty ingress array and strict egress whitelisting strictly bounds lateral movement, capping blast radius at or below 10 percent and blocking database port sweeps.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite! Base64 Kubernetes Secrets or load-balanced replicas do not restrict east-west pod network traffic. Only a Default-Deny NetworkPolicy on both Ingress and Egress with explicit port whitelists caps the cluster blast radius.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Interactive Lab 2: Multi-Layer Reliability and Continuous Authorization Simulator. Adjust independent security layers L, toggle Common-Mode credential coupling, and test Continuous Risk-Adaptive Authorization under live behavioral anomalies and session token decay.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check out Lab 2! Five independent layers bring breach odds down to 1 in 10 million—until you toggle Common-Mode credential sharing and watch conditional independence collapse!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Formative Checkpoint 2: SEC Form 8-K Four-Day Clock and Executive Criminal Liability. When does the mandatory SEC disclosure clock start, and what legal peril arises from masking payoffs as bug bounties?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Suppose forensics needs four weeks for packet reconstruction after confirming a material breach. Does the SEC 4-day clock wait, or does concealing via a bounty NDA create criminal exposure?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! SEC Item 1.05 starts ticking for four business days upon determining materiality—never waiting four weeks for complete forensic root cause. Disguising ransom behind fake NDAs risks DOJ conviction for obstruction and misprision of a felony.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Waiting four weeks for full packet capture forensics violates the strict four-business-day SEC materiality deadline, and disguising post-breach payoffs behind NDAs triggers criminal liability under Uber's DOJ precedent.
